## Project overview

Receipt Processor is a Python package and Streamlit application that turns
receipt images and PDFs into structured, searchable spending records. It
combines optical character recognition (OCR), locally run language-model
parsing, SQLite storage, and spending analytics to help make receipt data
useful for personal budgeting.

The project includes a hosted app, a Python package, and a documentation site
with a guided tutorial, API reference, and technical report.

## How it works

1. Receipt images or PDFs are processed with OCR to extract their text.
2. A locally hosted language model helps convert the unstructured text into
   receipt and item details, including dates, totals, descriptions, and
   categories.
3. The extracted information is stored in relational SQLite databases for
   receipts, items, budgets, and analysis.
4. The Streamlit interface supports uploading receipts, reviewing extracted
   information, making corrections, and exploring spending summaries.

The package also provides tools for analyzing spending by month, category, and
vendor, as well as tracking monthly and category budgets. Local LLM processing
was chosen to help keep sensitive receipt data on the user's own system.

## Tools and design

The project is built in Python and uses EasyOCR for text extraction,
Ollama-compatible local language models for parsing and categorization, SQLite
for data storage, and Streamlit for the interactive app. A validation workflow
compares extraction results with manually curated reference data to help
identify parsing errors.

Receipt layouts and OCR quality can vary. Unusual, multi-page, or refund
receipts may require manual review, and the spending analysis in the technical
report is based on a limited set of Walmart receipts rather than purchases
across all vendors.
